texts: bad: "burned dim" is taken as a resultative, so the parse adds a Result link asserting the burning caused the dimness — your sentence only says the lantern was dim while it burned. Split the two predications into finite clauses: "On day 120 of Year 1, a wraith emerged from the water of the Sunken Cove, because the Stilllight Lantern had burned on the night of day 111 and had been dim that night." Separately, "day 120 of Year 1" is stored with a day-of-month term, so a day-of-year count has no distinct reading for the translator — that is a coverage gap no rewrite avoids.

good. the repeated mention resolves to the same burning and the same emergence and adds the nine-day gap as a measured ordering beside the past-perfect one; the dimness itself rides on sentence 1's atoms, so keep this clause in step with whatever you do there ("had burned ... and had been dim nine days before the emergence").
good. the seeing, its experiencer and what was seen, the vantage point as a source, "first" as a rank on the seeing, and the station's possessor plus its position near the Cove Stair are all carried.
good. a plain past motion event with Marra as the walker and the lantern as the goal.

mixed: the position is recorded (Bevin at the lantern, in the past), but "already" survives nowhere — a bare "was at X" clause mints no event for the aspectual tag to hang on, so the earlier-than-expected timing drops out. If that timing matters, state it as a finite clause with the comparison spelled out: "Bevin Coombe had arrived at the Stilllight Lantern before Marra Tallowhand reached it."
good. the grinding, its agent and the feathers as a group the grinding changes are all covered.
good. "the ground feathers" resolves back to the feathers of the previous sentence, and the scattering keeps its agent, its theme and the "around the lantern" position.
good. the warding takes the feathers as agent, the lantern as what is warded and the wraith in an "against" slot, so all three participants are covered.
good. a plain past event with both participants covered.

bad: the particle is dropped — the event class comes out as plain "turn" and "away" appears nowhere, so the parse reads as the wraith turning at the lantern rather than turning away from it. Use a single-word verb so there is no particle to lose: "The wraith retreated from the Stilllight Lantern."
good. the denial wraps the whole draining bundle at strength zero while the lantern itself stays asserted outside it, which is the shape a later "did the wraith drain it?" question needs.
